data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A content-addressed derivation cache with durable provenance anchors achieves equivalent safety without requiring a global log, because evidence identity is decoupled from workspace location; the exact durable record is the (problem_id, input_hash, output_hash) provenance anchor.","counterconditions":[{"case":"Requires perfect determinism; any nondeterminism breaks the equivalence and can cause silent evidence loss","eval":"observation"},{"case":"Input data must remain available for recomputation","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The anchor record must be written atomically with respect to the evidence consumer","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The deterministic workspace implies reproducibility. The protocol durably records a provenance anchor mapping problem_id to (input_hash, output_hash) before declaring evidence complete. The actual workspace directory is treated as ephemeral scratch. Reclamation is always safe because there is no completed evidence in the workspace\u2014only a cache that can be rebuilt. Displacement of the workspace is therefore never displacement of evidence. The causal mechanism is the cryptographic commitment in the provenance anchor, which binds the evidence to its causal history independent of storage location. Adjudication: this dominates log-based protocols when input data is immutable and recomputation is cheaper than log coordination, but loses when determinism is imperfect.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
